newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong accord must be strictly observed-Blair.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong accord must be strictly observed-Blair.

text.p: Prime Minister Tony Blair on Wednesday stressed Britain's determination to ensure that the 1984 Joint Declaration with China on the future of Hong Kong is strictly observed.

Blair, speaking to parliament a day after returning from Hong Kong where he attended the handover ceremony to China, also said it was vital Britain use the accord on how the ex-colony is governed for the next 50 years to develop relations with Beijing.
"The basis of a strong and stable relationship with China, which we want, is adherence to the Joint Declaration," Blair told MPs at Prime Minister's Question Time.
"That is the basis of the freedoms of the people in Hong Kong, and that is the basis which we will expect to be adhered to."
Blair said it was of particular importance that elections should be held in Hong Kong within the next year.

"It is in the interests of Britain, of China and the people of Hong Kong that we make sure the joint declaration is kept to strictly, and we will, and secondly that we build upon that a strong and good relation with China for the future, and we will do that too," Blair said.
